text: Function because it's not something physical, right? You don't sense the power, but what you do is to set a counter, reset them value, and then you say if the counter is set to a value that is greater than zero, then you consider that the channel is busy, otherwise you say the channel is idle at the MAC layer. So we have a physical sensing function at the physical layer and a virtual sensing function at the MAC layer. Now clearly they may agree, right? They may both say channel busy or channel idle, but there are cases as we will see in which they may disagree. That means you sense something at the physical layer, so the physical layer says channel busy, and the MAC layer says channel idle, or vice versa. Okay, this may happen. So the protocol says a node will consider the channel as idle only if both the two carrier sensing functions say channel idle. Okay, so for the channel to be considered idle, you must have physical sensing say channel idle and the nav set to zero. That means MAC layer says also channel idle. Okay, if either one says channel busy, then you have to consider that the channel is busy. So in Wi-Fi we do use carrier sensing multiple access as a principle, but it's a bit more sophisticated than in other systems.
